title: Lesson 5: Communicating like a Human Biologist: Source Reliability & Academic Referencing
courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology

objectives.knowledge: Differentiate reliable peer-reviewed clinical evidence from non-scientific claims using the PROMT appraisal framework.
objectives.application: Apply strict Harvard referencing conventions (author-date in-text citations and full bibliography entries) to biomedical sources.
objectives.evaluation: Critically evaluate clinical data claims, detect methodological flaws and publication bias, and paraphrase complex bioscience findings without plagiarism.

terminology.def: Critical evaluation tool assessing Provenance, Relevance, Objectivity, Methodology, and Timeliness of scientific literature.
The selective publication of positive/favourable clinical results while burying negative or inconclusive trial findings.
Randomised Controlled Trial where neither participants nor researchers know who receives the experimental treatment vs placebo.
Author-date academic citation system requiring matching in-text signposts and an alphabetically ordered bibliography.
Re-articulating the core scientific meaning and findings in original structure and terminology rather than direct copying.

starterQuestions.q: What is the primary purpose of a clinical trial control group?
starterQuestions.a: To establish a baseline comparison to isolate the specific pharmacological effect of the experimental variable from placebo effect or natural disease progression.

starterQuestions.q: Name two variables that must be controlled in a blood test analysis.
starterQuestions.a: E.g., incubation temperature, sample storage time before centrifugation, anticoagulant type (e.g. EDTA vs heparin), or reagent concentration.

starterQuestions.q: Why is a large sample size critical in biomedical research?
starterQuestions.a: It maximizes statistical power, minimizes the distortion of random anomalies/biological variance, and narrows confidence intervals.

starterQuestions.q: Define quantitative data in the context of urinalysis.
starterQuestions.a: Numerical, measurable data with defined clinical units (e.g., glucose concentration in mmol/L or protein mg/dL) rather than descriptive/qualitative observations.

starterQuestions.q: What is the risk of using a biased sample in a drug trial?
starterQuestions.a: Produces unrepresentative results and skewed conclusions that fail to reflect the target patient population, risking ineffective treatment or hidden toxicity.

starterQuestions.q: How does peer review improve the reliability of scientific claims?
starterQuestions.a: Subjecting research methodology, statistical calculations, and data interpretation to scrutiny by independent experts (Review -> Feedback -> Correction) before publication.
